chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Musa, from his mother and the mother of Ahmad, daughter of Musa, said:

We were with Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) in the wilderness, and we intended to go to Baghdad. So he said to us on the day of Thursday: 'Wash for the day of tomorrow, the day of Friday, for the water there will be scarce tomorrow.' So we both washed on the day of Thursday for the day of Friday.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing the Friday ritual bath (Ghusl) on Thursday?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of 'Taqqaddum' (preemption) in Shia jurisprudence, where the obligatory Friday Ghusl is advanced to Thursday due to the specific necessity of water scarcity. It underscores the Imams' pragmatic approach to ritual law, demonstrating that the validity of the act is preserved even when performed outside its ideal time frame due to compelling environmental conditions.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Musa, from his mother and mother of Ahmad daughter of Musa, both said,

‘We were with Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> in the wilderness, and we intended to go to Baghdad. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to us on the day of Thursday: ‘Wash for the day of tomorrow, the day of Friday, for the water would be scarce tomorrow’. So we both washed on the day of Thursday for the day of Friday’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Musa from his mother, mother of Ahmad daughter of Musa who have said the following:

“We were with abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in the desert on our way to Baghdad. He (the Imam) said to us, ‘Today is Thursday, take Ghusl (bath) for Friday, tomorrow water will be scarce.’ We took Ghusl (bath) on Thursday for Friday.’”
